newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end softer with U.S. in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end softer with U.S. in quiet market.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in quiet trading on Monday, pulled lower by weaker U.S. Treasuries amid a lack of significant economic news or data, analysts said.

"We didn't have any new issues. We didn't have any particular economic numbers to move our market," said David Yu, fixed-income porfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "I think we just followed the U.S. lead."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.55 to C$109.00 to yield 7.230 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 17/32 to yield 6.78 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed 45 basis points from 46 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds opened weaker this morning, with markets seen as defensive ahead of employment data being released Friday on both sides of the border. Traders said the reports are expected to play a key role in the timing of next interest rate moves by Canadian and U.S. central banks.

"It's a bit early, but I think traders are already focusing on the weight of the non-farm jobs reports, both for Canada and the U.S.," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with financial analysis firm Technical Data.
Canadian foreign reserves data released this morning had little impact on prices, dealers said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent due 2006 fell C$0.35 to C$102.85 to yield 6.602 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to six basis points from four basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.86 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.17 percent.
